chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A slave girl of mine was pregnant, so I vowed for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that if she gave birth to a boy, I would send him for Hajj or perform Hajj on his behalf.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A man vowed for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding a son of his, that if he reached maturity, he would either perform Hajj on his behalf or send him. The father died, and the boy reached maturity afterwards. The boy came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him about that. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that he should perform Hajj on his behalf, from what his father had left.'

key_terms.أَحُجَّ عَنْهُ: I would perform Hajj on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father's vow to perform Hajj for his minor son if the father dies before the son matures?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of vow fulfillment (nadhr) when the obligor dies before the condition is met, establishing that the debt transfers to the heir using the deceased's estate. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the vow remains binding on the individual once they reach maturity, rather than being extinguished by the father's death, ensuring the spiritual obligation is discharged from the father's assets.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Misma’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There was a slave girl of mine who was pregnant. So I vowed for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that if she were to give birth to a boy, I would send him for Hajj, or I would perform Hajj on his behalf’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man vowed for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic regarding a son of his, that when he is mature he would either perform Hajj of his behalf, or send him to Hajj. So the father dies and the boy matured afterwards. So the boy came to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, to ask him<sup>saww</sup> about that. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ordered him that he should perform Hajj on his behalf, from what his father had neglected’.
en.sarwar: 25. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Misma‘ who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of my girl who was pregnant and I made a vow and commitment for Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, that if she gives birth to a boy, I will help him to perform al-Hajj or I will perform al-Hajj on his behalf.

He (the Imam) said, ‘A man made a vow and commitment for Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, about his son that if he matures he will perform al-Hajj for him or help him to perform al-Hajj. The father died and the boy became mature thereafter and came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, who commanded him to perform al-Hajj by means of what his father has left behind.’”
